prompt: ​"The availability of entertainment such as video games on handheld devices is harmful to individuals and the society they live in. To what extent do you agree or disagree?"
essay:
It is often argued that the widespread availability of online video games on mobile devices poses significant disadvantages to individuals and society. While I acknowledge that gaming can foster certain cognitive and language skills, I largely agree that its negative impacts on health, productivity, and social cohesion are far more damaging.

​On the one hand, mobile video games offer a few notable benefits. Firstly, engaging in multiplayer online games allows players to develop teamwork and communication skills, as they often collaborate with people from diverse cultural backgrounds. This experience can also enhance foreign language proficiency through real-time interaction. Furthermore, strategic games can sharpen problem-solving abilities and broaden cognitive horizons. However, these benefits are only realized when gaming is done in moderation.

​On the other hand, the drawbacks of accessible handheld gaming heavily outweigh these advantages. The primary issue is addiction, which leads to a severe waste of time and reduced productivity. Many individuals, especially young adults, struggle to manage their daily schedules effectively, neglecting their studies or professional responsibilities. Moreover, modern video games often rely on microtransactions and in-game purchases that can incur exorbitant costs, putting financial pressure on players and their families. Consequently, excessive gaming contributes to physical health problems, such as a sedentary lifestyle, and weakens real-world social bonds.

​In conclusion, although mobile video games can provide recreational value and skill development if controlled, their potential to cause addiction, financial strain, and social isolation makes them overall detrimental. Therefore, individuals should strictly regulate their screen time to ensure a balanced lifestyle.
